q: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally commissioned by the emperor:
e: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, one of the oldest stone structures in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was originally commissioned by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.

q: Fatehpur Sikri, the city founded near Agra which briefly served as the Mughal capital, was built by:
e: Fatehpur Sikri, the red sandstone city near Agra that served briefly as the Mughal capital, was built by the emperor Akbar to honour the Sufi saint Salim Chishti.

q: The famous Meenakshi Temple, known for its tall sculptured gopurams, is located at:
e: The Meenakshi Temple, famous for its tall sculptured gopurams covered with colourful figures, is located at Madurai in Tamil Nadu and is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareswarar.

q: Silent Valley National Park, known for its evergreen tropical forests, is located in the State of:
e: Silent Valley National Park, preserving one of the last undisturbed tracts of tropical evergreen forest in the Nilgiri hills, is located in Kerala.

q: Namdapha National Park, one of the largest protected areas of India, is located in:
e: Namdapha National Park, a vast protected area in the Changlang district with tigers, leopards and hoolock gibbons, is located in Arunachal Pradesh.

q: Dachigam National Park, known for the hangul (Kashmir stag), is located in:
e: Dachigam National Park near Srinagar, famous as the main home of the endangered hangul or Kashmir stag, is located in Jammu and Kashmir.

q: Khardung La, among the highest motorable mountain passes of the world, is located in:
e: Khardung La, one of the highest motorable passes in the world at about 5,359 metres, is located in Ladakh on the road from Leh towards the Nubra valley.

q: The Lipulekh Pass, on the route of the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage, is located in the State of:
e: The Lipulekh Pass, in the Pithoragarh district on the traditional route of the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage, is located in Uttarakhand.

q: The capital of Arunachal Pradesh is:
e: Itanagar, situated in the foothills of the Himalayas in the Papum Pare district, is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh.

q: A crescograph, invented by Jagadish Chandra Bose, is an instrument used to measure:
e: The crescograph, invented by Jagadish Chandra Bose, magnifies and records the minute movements of plants and is used to measure plant growth.

q: The equity of the Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited (MRVC) is shared between the Ministry of Railways and the Government of Maharashtra in the ratio of:
e: In Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited, the Ministry of Railways holds 51 per cent equity and the Government of Maharashtra 49 per cent, making it a Railways-majority joint venture.

q: IRCON International Limited was granted the 'Navratna' status in October 2023, becoming which numbered Navratna company among the Central Public Sector Enterprises?
e: IRCON International Limited became the 15th Navratna CPSE when the Ministry of Finance granted it Navratna status in October 2023, with RITES following as the 16th.

q: The National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC), which implements the Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridors, is a joint venture of the Government of India with the State Governments of:

options.A: Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh
options.D: Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Haryana

e: The National Capital Region Transport Corporation is a joint venture of the Government of India with the State Governments of Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh for implementing RRTS corridors.

q: In the Rail Infrastructure Development Company (Karnataka) Limited (K-RIDE), which implements the Bengaluru Suburban Rail Project, the majority equity stake of 51 per cent is held by the:
e: In K-RIDE, which implements the Bengaluru Suburban Rail Project, the Government of Karnataka holds the majority 51 per cent equity stake, with the Ministry of Railways holding the rest.

q: The Maharashtra Rail Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (MRIDC), a joint venture of the Government of Maharashtra and the Ministry of Railways, is popularly known as:
e: The Maharashtra Rail Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited, a joint venture of the Government of Maharashtra and the Ministry of Railways, is popularly known as MahaRail.

q: The Haryana Rail Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (HRIDC) is the implementing authority for which rail project in Haryana?

options.C: Haryana Orbital Rail Corridor from Palwal to Sonipat

e: The Haryana Rail Infrastructure Development Corporation is the implementing authority for the Haryana Orbital Rail Corridor running from Palwal to Sonipat around Delhi.

q: The High Speed Rail Training Institute, being set up by the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited to train the staff for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor, is located at:
e: The High Speed Rail Training Institute for staff of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor is being set up by NHSRCL at Vadodara, alongside the National Academy of Indian Railways.

q: Under the Nirbhaya Fund, the work of providing the Internet Protocol based Video Surveillance System (VSS) with video analytics at railway stations has been entrusted to:
e: Under the Nirbhaya Fund, the work of providing IP-based Video Surveillance Systems with video analytics at railway stations has been entrusted to RailTel Corporation of India Limited.

q: The 'Rail Drishti' dashboard, which brings information on train movement, punctuality, earnings, freight loading and major projects of Indian Railways on a single platform, has been developed by the:

options.D: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

e: The Rail Drishti dashboard, presenting train movement, punctuality, earnings, freight loading and project information on one platform, was developed by CRIS, the Railways IT arm.

q: The 125-km long Rishikesh-Karnaprayag new railway line in Uttarakhand, which will improve rail connectivity towards the Char Dham region, is being executed by:

options.B: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited
options.D: National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited

e: The 125-km Rishikesh-Karnaprayag new line in Uttarakhand, improving rail access towards the Char Dham region, is being executed by Rail Vikas Nigam Limited.

q: Under a contract secured in 2023, RITES Limited is supplying ten 3,300 HP Cape Gauge diesel-electric locomotives, manufactured at the Banaras Locomotive Works, to the railway operator CFM of:
e: Under a contract secured in 2023, RITES is supplying ten 3,300 HP Cape Gauge diesel-electric locomotives built at Banaras Locomotive Works to CFM, the railway operator of Mozambique.

q: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has equal equity participation of the:

options.A: Government of India and Government of Haryana
options.B: Government of India and Government of NCT of Delhi
options.C: Government of NCT of Delhi and Government of Uttar Pradesh
options.D: Government of India and Government of Punjab

e: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation has equal equity participation of the Government of India and the Government of NCT of Delhi, each holding 50 per cent.

q: Besides borrowing funds from the market to finance the acquisition of rolling stock which is leased to Indian Railways, the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) also provides financial assistance by way of loans to:

options.A: Other railway sector entities such as RVNL, RailTel and Konkan Railway Corporation

e: Besides financing rolling stock leased to Indian Railways, IRFC also lends to other railway sector entities such as RVNL, RailTel and Konkan Railway Corporation.

q: The West Central Railway, with headquarters at Jabalpur, came into existence on:
e: The West Central Railway, headquartered at Jabalpur and carved out of Central and Western Railway territories, came into existence on 1 April 2003.

q: The Signal and Telecommunication Workshop at Podanur, which manufactures signalling relays, point machines and axle counters for the entire Indian Railways, belongs to the:
e: The Signal and Telecommunication Workshop at Podanur, which makes signalling relays, point machines and axle counters for Indian Railways, belongs to the Southern Railway.

q: The Central Workshop at Ashokapuram, Mysuru, which undertakes periodic overhaul of broad gauge coaches including LHB coaches, functions under the:
e: The Central Workshop at Ashokapuram, Mysuru, which undertakes periodic overhaul of broad gauge coaches including LHB coaches, functions under the South Western Railway.

q: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Mancheswar, Bhubaneswar, whose first periodically overhauled coach was turned out in December 1983, functions under the:
e: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Mancheswar, Bhubaneswar, which turned out its first overhauled coach in December 1983, functions under the East Coast Railway.

q: The Traction Machine Workshop at Nasik Road, which undertakes repair and rewinding of traction motors of electric locomotives and EMUs, belongs to the:
e: The Traction Machine Workshop at Nasik Road, repairing and rewinding traction motors of electric locomotives and EMUs, belongs to the Central Railway.

q: The railway unit at Kazipet in Telangana, originally sanctioned as a wagon periodic-overhaul workshop, was upgraded in 2023 into a railway manufacturing unit for the manufacture of:
e: The Kazipet unit in Telangana, originally sanctioned as a wagon periodic-overhaul workshop for 200 wagons a month, was upgraded in 2023 into a railway manufacturing unit for manufacture of wagons.

q: The Carriage Workshop at Lallaguda, Secunderabad, now a major coach workshop of the South Central Railway, had its origin in 1893 as a workshop of the:
e: The Carriage Workshop at Lallaguda, Secunderabad, now a major South Central Railway coach workshop, originated in 1893 as a workshop of the Nizam's Guaranteed State Railway.

q: The periodic overhaul (POH) of the EMU rakes of the Mumbai suburban section of Western Railway is carried out at the EMU Workshop located at:
e: Periodic overhaul of EMU rakes of the Mumbai suburban section of Western Railway is carried out at the EMU Workshop at Mahalaxmi in Mumbai.

q: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Alambagh, Lucknow, one of the major coach workshops of Indian Railways, functions under the:
e: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Alambagh, Lucknow, one of the major coach workshops of Indian Railways, functions under the Northern Railway.

q: The Marathwada Rail Coach Factory at Latur, commissioned in December 2020 with the production of its first coach shell, has been designed to manufacture:

options.C: Advanced coaches such as MEMU, EMU, LHB and train sets

e: The Marathwada Rail Coach Factory at Latur, commissioned in December 2020 with its first coach shell, is designed to manufacture advanced coaches such as MEMU, EMU, LHB coaches and train sets.

q: The Zonal Railway Training Institute (ZRTI) at Udaipur functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Udaipur, which trains subordinate staff of the zone, functions under the North Western Railway.

q: In Indian Railways, 'TCAS', the train protection technology earlier adopted under this name before being developed as the Kavach system, stands for:
e: TCAS stands for Train Collision Avoidance System, the indigenous train protection technology that was further developed and adopted as the Kavach system.

q: In the context of the provident fund maintained for railway employees, 'GPF' stands for:
e: GPF stands for General Provident Fund, the provident fund maintained for government and railway employees to which they subscribe during service.

q: In railway pension matters, the document 'PPO' issued in favour of a pensioner stands for:
e: PPO stands for Pension Payment Order, the document issued to a retiring employee authorising payment of pension and other retirement benefits.

q: In railway leave rules, 'LHAP' stands for:

options.D: Leave for Hospital and Allied Purposes

e: LHAP stands for Leave on Half Average Pay, the leave admissible to railway employees, commonly used for medical and private purposes under the leave rules.

q: In railway works and stores contracts, the 'LOA' issued to the successful bidder stands for:
e: LOA stands for Letter of Acceptance, the letter issued to the successful bidder in works and stores contracts confirming acceptance of the tender and forming the basis of the contract.

q: In railway tendering, the abbreviation 'NIT' stands for:
e: NIT stands for Notice Inviting Tender, the published notice through which bids are invited from contractors or suppliers for a work or supply.

q: In railway freight policy, the scheme 'LWIS', under which customers invest in the procurement of wagons for carrying their traffic, stands for:
e: LWIS stands for Liberalised Wagon Investment Scheme, under which freight customers invest in procuring wagons for carrying their own traffic and earn freight rebates.

q: In railway freight business, a 'PFT' developed by a private party for handling rail cargo stands for:
e: PFT stands for Private Freight Terminal, a terminal developed by a private party on private land for handling rail-borne cargo under the Railways policy.

q: In railway signalling and train operations, the system 'CTC' provided on busy sections for controlling trains from a central place stands for:
e: CTC stands for Centralised Traffic Control, the signalling system by which trains on a busy section are controlled and monitored from a central control office.

q: In railway commercial working, an 'SPTM' installed at stations for issuing unreserved tickets stands for:
e: SPTM stands for Self Printing Ticket Machine, the machine installed at stations through which passengers themselves obtain unreserved tickets.

q: In railway freight operations, the device 'EoTT' fitted at the end of a freight train stands for:
e: EoTT stands for End of Train Telemetry, the device fitted at the end of a freight train that transmits brake-pipe pressure and train integrity information to the locomotive.

q: The 'RailOne' application launched by Indian Railways in July 2025 is best described as:

options.A: An application only for booking unreserved tickets
options.B: An application only for booking freight rakes
options.C: An application only for railway employees
options.D: A super app integrating ticketing, live train tracking, grievance redressal, e-catering, porter booking and other passenger services on a single platform

e: RailOne, launched in July 2025, is a super app integrating reserved and unreserved ticketing, live train tracking, grievance redressal, e-catering, porter booking and other passenger services on one platform.

q: 'Operation Matrishakti' of the Railway Protection Force is an initiative for:

options.A: Assisting pregnant women passengers who go into labour during train journeys
options.B: Rescuing children in need of care and protection at stations
options.C: Checking ticketless travel in ladies compartments
options.D: Providing free food to women passengers in trains

e: Operation Matrishakti of the RPF is the initiative under which women personnel assist pregnant women passengers who go into labour during train journeys.

q: 'Operation Narcos' of the Railway Protection Force is directed mainly against:

options.A: Theft of railway property from goods sheds
options.B: Smuggling of narcotics and drugs through the railways
options.C: Unauthorised entry of passengers into reserved coaches
options.D: Touting of reserved tickets at stations

e: Operation Narcos of the RPF is directed mainly against smuggling of narcotics and drugs through the railways, carried out with checks on trains and stations.

q: The 'Mitali Express', the third passenger train service between India and Bangladesh, which commenced regular service in June 2022, connects New Jalpaiguri with:
e: The Mitali Express, the third passenger train between India and Bangladesh which began regular service in June 2022, connects New Jalpaiguri with Dhaka.

q: The cross-border rail link inaugurated in November 2023, which provided the first rail connectivity between Bangladesh and the North-East, connects Agartala in Tripura with:
e: The cross-border rail link inaugurated in November 2023, giving Bangladesh its first rail connectivity with the North-East, connects Agartala in Tripura with Akhaura in Bangladesh.

q: 'Project Utkrisht', launched by Indian Railways in April 2018, mainly relates to:

options.A: Construction of new railway stations in district headquarters
options.B: Upgradation of ICF-design coaches of Mail and Express trains with improved interiors, toilets and passenger amenities
options.C: Manufacture of Vande Bharat train sets in production units

e: Project Utkrisht, launched in April 2018, relates to upgradation of ICF-design coaches of Mail and Express trains with improved interiors, toilets and passenger amenities.

q: As a system improvement, the Ministry of Railways introduced the system of publishing an annual calendar for recruitment to various categories of Group 'C' posts from the year:
e: As a system improvement, the Ministry of Railways introduced the system of publishing an annual calendar for recruitment to various Group C categories from the year 2024, so that examinations follow a fixed yearly schedule.

q: The first 'Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal' of Indian Railways, commissioned in March 2022 at the Maithan Power Limited siding at Thaparnagar, falls under which division of Eastern Railway?
e: The first Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal, commissioned in March 2022 at the Maithan Power Limited siding at Thaparnagar, falls under the Asansol division of Eastern Railway.

q: Under the first-ever rail links between India and Bhutan announced in September 2025, the Kokrajhar-Gelephu line will connect Kokrajhar in Assam with Gelephu, which is located in:
e: Under the first India-Bhutan rail links announced in September 2025, the Kokrajhar-Gelephu line will connect Kokrajhar in Assam with Gelephu, which is located in Bhutan.

q: 'Yatri Mitra Sewa', introduced at major railway stations and entrusted to IRCTC, mainly enables elderly, ailing and differently-abled passengers to book:

options.B: Free meals during the train journey
options.C: Tatkal tickets without payment of premium charges

e: Yatri Mitra Sewa, entrusted to IRCTC at major stations, enables elderly, ailing and differently-abled passengers to book wheelchair-cum-porter services at stations.

q: The novel 'The Guide', in which the hero Raju becomes a reluctant holy man, was written by:
e: The Guide, in which tour guide Raju becomes a reluctant holy man after his release from jail, was written by R. K. Narayan and later adapted into the film Guide.

q: The Hindi novel 'Godaan', regarded as a classic on the life of Indian peasants, was written by:
e: Godaan, the Hindi novel portraying the suffering of the peasant Hori and his family, was written by Munshi Premchand and is regarded as his masterpiece.

q: The novel 'The Home and the World' (Ghare Baire), set against the Swadeshi movement, was written by:
e: The Home and the World, or Ghare Baire, set against the Swadeshi movement with Nikhil, Sandip and Bimala as central figures, was written by Rabindranath Tagore.

q: The book 'India After Gandhi', a widely read history of India since Independence, was written by:
e: India After Gandhi, a widely read history of India since Independence in 1947, was written by Ramachandra Guha and published in 2007.

q: The novel 'Five Point Someone', set in an IIT hostel, was written by:
e: Five Point Someone, the novel set in an IIT hostel about Hari, Ryan and Alok, was the debut novel of Chetan Bhagat, published in 2004.

q: The novel 'The Glass Palace', set largely in Burma and Malaya, was written by:
e: The Glass Palace, tracing a Burmese teak trader's family across Burma, India and Malaya from the fall of Mandalay onwards, was written by Amitav Ghosh.

q: The novel 'David Copperfield', considered the most autobiographical of its author's works, was written by:
e: David Copperfield, the novel following its hero from childhood to maturity and considered the most autobiographical of its author's works, was written by Charles Dickens.

q: The novella 'Heart of Darkness', set on the Congo River in Africa, was written by:
e: Heart of Darkness, the novella in which Marlow journeys up the Congo River in search of Kurtz, was written by Joseph Conrad and published in 1899.

q: The novel 'Ulysses', set in Dublin over a single day, was written by:
e: Ulysses, set in Dublin over a single day, 16 June 1904, and following Leopold Bloom, was written by the Irish author James Joyce.

q: The novel 'Mrs Dalloway', known for its stream-of-consciousness narration, was written by:
e: Mrs Dalloway, which follows Clarissa Dalloway through one day in London using stream-of-consciousness narration, was written by Virginia Woolf.

q: The novel 'The Grapes of Wrath', about migrant farm workers during the Great Depression, was written by:
e: The Grapes of Wrath, about the Joad family of migrant farm workers during the Great Depression, was written by John Steinbeck and won the Pulitzer Prize.

q: The novel 'Gone with the Wind', set during the American Civil War, was written by:
e: Gone with the Wind, set in Georgia during the American Civil War and centred on Scarlett O'Hara, was written by Margaret Mitchell and published in 1936.

q: The novel 'Doctor Zhivago', which earned its author the Nobel Prize in Literature, was written by:
e: Doctor Zhivago, the novel about Yuri Zhivago set against the Russian Revolution, was written by Boris Pasternak, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1958.

q: The novel 'The Brothers Karamazov', a philosophical novel on faith and morality, was written by:
e: The Brothers Karamazov, the philosophical novel on faith, morality and the three Karamazov brothers, was the last novel of Fyodor Dostoevsky.

q: The adventure novel 'The Three Musketeers', featuring d'Artagnan and the musketeers, was written by:
e: The Three Musketeers, the adventure novel featuring d'Artagnan with Athos, Porthos and Aramis, was written by the French author Alexandre Dumas.

q: The play 'Faust', the story of a scholar who makes a pact with the devil, was written by:
e: Faust, the play about the scholar Faust who makes a pact with Mephistopheles, was written by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Germany's greatest literary figure.

q: The book 'On the Origin of Species' (1859), which presented the theory of evolution by natural selection, was written by:
e: On the Origin of Species, published in 1859, presented Charles Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection based on his studies including the Galapagos voyage.

q: The First Backward Classes Commission (1953) was chaired by:
e: The First Backward Classes Commission, appointed in 1953 under Article 340, was chaired by Kaka Kalelkar and is known as the Kaka Kalelkar Commission.

q: The Janakiraman Committee (1992) was set up by the Reserve Bank of India to enquire into:

options.A: The working of the lead bank scheme
options.B: The licensing of new private banks
options.C: Securities transactions of banks and financial institutions
options.D: The merger of weak public sector banks

e: The Janakiraman Committee of 1992 was set up by the Reserve Bank of India to enquire into securities transactions of banks and financial institutions, following the securities scam.

q: The Malegam Committee (2011), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, is associated with the study of:
e: The Malegam Committee of 2011, appointed by the Reserve Bank of India and chaired by Y. H. Malegam, studied microfinance institutions and recommended their regulation as NBFC-MFIs.

q: The Chore Committee (1979), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, reviewed:

options.B: The branch licensing policy of banks
options.D: The system of cash credit in banks

e: The Chore Committee of 1979, appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, reviewed the system of cash credit in banks and recommended measures to discipline working capital finance.

q: The Mashelkar Committee (2002-03) is associated with the formulation of the:
e: The Mashelkar Committee of 2002-03, chaired by R. A. Mashelkar, is associated with the formulation of the National Auto Fuel Policy covering vehicle and fuel norms.

q: The Shanta Kumar Committee (2015) was set up to recommend the restructuring of:
e: The Shanta Kumar Committee of 2015 was set up to recommend restructuring of the Food Corporation of India, including its procurement, storage and distribution functions.

q: The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income (2016) was chaired by:
e: The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income, constituted in 2016 to suggest how farm incomes could be doubled by 2022, was chaired by Ashok Dalwai.

q: The Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel (2011) was chaired by:
e: The Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel of 2011, whose report recommended ecologically sensitive zoning of the Western Ghats, was chaired by Madhav Gadgil.

q: The L. M. Singhvi Committee (1986) is associated with recommendations on:

options.B: The revitalisation of Panchayati Raj institutions
options.C: The reorganisation of State transport undertakings

e: The L. M. Singhvi Committee of 1986 recommended revitalisation of Panchayati Raj institutions and constitutional status for them, paving the way for the 73rd Amendment.

q: The Commission headed by Justice G. Rohini (2017) was appointed to examine:

options.A: The reservation of seats in legislatures
options.B: The pay structure of Central Government employees
options.C: The working of the National Commission for Women
options.D: The sub-categorisation of Other Backward Classes

e: The Commission headed by Justice G. Rohini, appointed in 2017, was set up to examine the sub-categorisation of Other Backward Classes in the central list.

q: The first SEBI Committee on Corporate Governance (1999) was chaired by:
e: The first SEBI Committee on Corporate Governance, constituted in 1999, was chaired by Kumar Mangalam Birla and recommended governance norms for listed companies.

q: Odissi is a classical dance form of the State of:
e: Odissi, with its distinctive tribhangi posture and themes from the Jagannath cult and the Gita Govinda, is the classical dance form of Odisha.

q: Manipuri, known for its graceful Ras Leela performances, is a classical dance form of the State of:
e: Manipuri, known for its graceful movements and Ras Leela performances centred on Radha and Krishna, is the classical dance form of Manipur.

q: Lohri, the bonfire festival marking the end of the winter season, is celebrated mainly in the State of:
e: Lohri, the bonfire festival celebrated on the eve of Makar Sankranti marking the end of winter and the harvest of rabi crops, is celebrated mainly in Punjab.

q: Bathukamma, the festival of flowers celebrated by women, is the State festival of:
e: Bathukamma, the nine-day festival of flowers in which women worship Goddess Gauri with floral arrangements, is the State festival of Telangana.

q: Ottawa is the capital of:
e: Ottawa, situated in Ontario on the Ottawa River, is the capital of Canada and seat of its federal government and Parliament.

q: Wellington is the capital of:
e: Wellington, located at the southern tip of the North Island, is the capital of New Zealand and seat of its Parliament.

q: The Dhuandhar Falls, near Jabalpur, are formed by the river:
e: The Dhuandhar Falls, where the river plunges through the marble rocks near Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh, are formed by the Narmada river.

q: The Shivanasamudra Falls, among the earliest sites of hydroelectric power in Asia, are formed by the river:
e: The Shivanasamudra Falls, among the earliest hydroelectric sites in Asia with a station set up in 1902, are formed by the Kaveri river in Karnataka.

q: Lonar Lake, formed in a crater created by a meteorite impact, is located in the State of:
e: Lonar Lake, a saline crater lake formed by a meteorite impact in basalt rock in the Buldhana district, is located in Maharashtra.

q: Kolleru Lake, one of the largest freshwater lakes of India lying between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, is located in the State of:
e: Kolleru Lake, one of India's largest freshwater lakes lying between the Krishna and Godavari deltas and a Ramsar site, is located in Andhra Pradesh.

q: In the Battle of Chausa (1539), the Mughal emperor Humayun was defeated by:
e: In the Battle of Chausa in 1539, the Mughal emperor Humayun was defeated by Sher Shah Suri, forcing Humayun to flee and lose his empire for a period.

q: In the Battle of Samugarh (1658), fought during the Mughal war of succession, Dara Shikoh was defeated by:
e: In the Battle of Samugarh in 1658, fought during the Mughal war of succession, Aurangzeb defeated Dara Shikoh and moved decisively towards the throne.

q: 'Alam Ara', released in 1931, is remembered in Indian cinema as the:
e: Alam Ara, released in 1931 and directed by Ardeshir Irani, is remembered as the first Indian talkie film, beginning the era of sound in Indian cinema.

q: Justice Leila Seth is remembered as the first woman to become:

options.A: A judge of the Delhi High Court
options.C: Chief Justice of a High Court in India

e: Justice Leila Seth is remembered as the first woman to become Chief Justice of a High Court in India, when she headed the Himachal Pradesh High Court in 1991.

q: The Ramappa Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva and noted for its floating bricks, is located in the State of:
e: The Ramappa Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva and noted for its lightweight floating bricks, is located at Palampet in Telangana and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: Pattadakal, a group of Chalukya-era temples and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in the State of:
e: Pattadakal, a group of Chalukya-era temples blending Nagara and Dravidian styles and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in Karnataka.

q: The Borra Caves, famous limestone caves in the Ananthagiri hills near Araku Valley, are located in the State of:
e: The Borra Caves, famous limestone caves with stalactite and stalagmite formations in the Ananthagiri hills near Araku Valley, are located in Andhra Pradesh.
